images.caption: Figure 2:Method overview.(a) Instead of jointly generating a fixed-length clip, the model generates state transitions causally and ends with a visual EOS frame. (b) The decision-focused schedule moves training to high noise levels, where the next state is hidden and must be inferred from the rules and the history. (c) From the state𝐡d\mathbf{h}_{d}before a failed decision, CFT resamples a successful continuation and trains the noiseϵd−\boldsymbol{\epsilon}^{-}_{d}that produced the failed decision to generate the successful decision𝐗d+\mathbf{X}^{+}_{d}, shifting the decision distribution toward solvable moves.

Figure 3:Qualitative comparison of generation paradigmson one test puzzle per benchmark. The first four columns show the same frame indexttin every row, and the last column shows each model’s EOS frame (red border). Orange borders mark rule violations.
Figure 7:Out-of-distribution results.Our models generalize to a larger puzzle (a) and a new layout (b).

Figure S1:Test examples of the three benchmarks.For each task, we show the first frame, the middle frame, and the last frame of the reference video. Every video ends with EOS frames that repeat the final state with a red border.

Figure S3:Two divergence points of the probe in Fig.6, at which the failed rollout (a) reaches a dead end and (b) hallucinates. Left: the last frame of the shared history, the successful move, and the failing move, shown in (b) two moves later, where the failure becomes visible. Right: the share of 32 fresh noises with which each model generates the successful decision, the failing decision, or another move.
Figure S6:Comparison with HDR and S2PDon one test puzzle per benchmark. Orange borders mark rule violations.
Figure S7:More comparisons of the generation paradigmson two tasks not included in Fig.3. Orange borders mark rule violations, and the last column shows the final frame of each video.

Figure S8:Qualitative results of (a) the decision-focused scheduleon RoboTwin-Planand (b) post-trainingon VBVR-MultiStep. Orange borders mark rule violations, and the last column shows the final frame of each video.

Figure S9:Long-horizon solutions.The longest strictly successful videos of our models, with frames evenly spaced from the first frame to the EOS frame. The longest expert videos last 15.8 s on Sokoban, 11.6 s on Blocks World, 10.8 s on FlowFree, and 12.1 s on Tower of Hanoi.
